evidence: buy(): calls boxOffice.purchase(...) and maps the result to { code, total: euros(result.totalCents) }, which is response mapping and display formatting
events(): maps boxOffice.listing() entries to DTOs using e.remaining() and euros(e.priceCents); the remaining-seat calculation lives in the domain
scan(): calls boxOffice.admit(body.code) and then gates.scanned(ticket.code, body.gate), a sequence of calls with no branching or rules; borderline, but acceptable for a controller
BuyBody/ScanBody are interfaces describing request bodies, which belongs in presentation
parsedVerdict.reasoning: TicketController does the work of a presentation-layer controller. It defines the request body shapes (BuyBody, ScanBody), hands each operation to the business services BoxOffice and GateLog, and maps the results to response objects. Money is formatted for display through the presentation helper euros(). The file has no persistence logic, such as storage access or queries. It also contains no pricing, seat-availability or validation rules: totalCents, remaining() and priceCents are all computed in the business layer. scan() is borderline because it chains two business calls, boxOffice.admit followed by gates.scanned. That chain could be moved into a business use case. But it holds no decision logic, only a straight sequence of calls, which is ordinary for a thin controller. It is not a clearly misplaced business rule.
